children: The FTSE MIB edged up 0.3% to 52,230 on Monday amid several macroeconomic developments.
Talks over contributions from banks and energy firms to help fill the government’s budget shortfall continued over the weekend.
Energy stocks outperformed, tracking higher oil prices, led by Tenaris (1.1%).
Heavyweight financials were mixed, while the banking sector remained in focus ahead of Intesa’s shareholder meeting on Thursday to approve the capital increase for MPS’s takeover.
Stellantis rose 0.4% while Canadian tariffs on US goods are set to take effect on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Italy recorded its hottest summer since 1950, pointing to increased demand for electricity used for cooling, although continued tensions in the Middle East threaten firms’ margins by pushing European gas prices higher.
Defense contractor Leonardo declined 0.5% after signing a production contract for the Brazilian army.

title: FTSE MIB Inches Higher
